transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep feeling like I’ve ruined things for everyone. Like I’m a fake in my apprenticeship, and I’ve let my family and the younger apprentices down over mistakes that other people would probably just fix and move on from.
When did you first start feeling this way, and did it begin around the same time as any particular event or change in your life?
It started about five months ago, around when I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship. That’s when this whole pattern really started.
Over the past several weeks, have you been feeling sad, down, or empty for most of the day, nearly every day, or have you noticed you no longer enjoy things you used to?

I’m not really enjoying the things I usually do. I’ll walk past my sketchbook, skip volleyball, ignore the volunteer group texts... and I just don’t feel much about it, even though those things used to make me feel like myself.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah. For a while I was only getting three or four hours and still felt wired enough to go to work and class. Now it’s more that I can’t fall asleep, or I wake up before my alarm feeling like I didn’t rest at all.

During that time when you were only sleeping three or four hours but still felt wired, did you also notice your mood or energy feeling unusually high, elevated, or irritable, or more like you were unusually productive or full of ideas?

Yeah, I had this nonstop charge in my body. Even after a full day working on pipes, I’d go to evening class, reorganize all my tools, clean my apartment, and start drawing out systems instead of just sitting down.
How many days in a row did that period of high energy and needing less sleep last?
It’s been going on for about five months, since I started the sustainable plumbing certification along with my apprenticeship.

Did that period of high energy and reduced need for sleep come to an end before you started feeling low and losing interest in things, or have both the high-energy feelings and the low, unmotivated feelings been happening together at the same time?

They’ve kind of been happening together. Lately I just walk past my sketchbook, skip volleyball, ignore the volunteer group texts—things that used to make me feel like myself—and I don’t really feel much about it.

During this period, have you noticed your thoughts racing, felt unusually confident or like you could do more than others expect of you, or found yourself making impulsive decisions you wouldn't normally make?

Yeah—my thoughts were jumping all over. I’d be thinking about pipe layouts, then a business plan, then texting classmates, then fixing my mom’s bathroom, all at once. I couldn’t slow it down enough to just focus on one thing.

During this period of high energy and racing thoughts, has it caused serious problems—like conflicts at work, financial or relationship trouble, or something that made others worried enough to intervene—or has it mostly been noticeable to you without major disruption to your daily life?

It’s caused problems at work and school. My instructors and my foreman have had to keep chasing me about unfinished sketches and that my work’s gotten slower. I’m honestly scared I’m going to mess up the apprenticeship and certification I worked really hard to get.

Over the past five months, has there been a period of at least one full week where you had both this high-energy, racing-thoughts feeling and the low, unmotivated feeling happening together nearly every day, or has it been more on-and-off, with days that don't clearly fit either pattern?
It’s been going on for about five months now. It started after I took on the sustainable plumbing certification along with my apprenticeship.

During this period, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds others don't hear, or having beliefs that others tell you aren't true or don't make sense—like feeling you have special powers or that people are plotting against you?
No, I haven’t experienced anything like that.

Focusing on the last few weeks specifically, can you tell me if there was a stretch of at least seven days in a row where you had both the high-energy, racing-thoughts feeling and the low, unmotivated feeling every single day, without a break in between?
It’s been pretty continuous for about five months, since I started the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but sometimes driving home after class or lying awake, I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow.
